clue.text: Coastal defence that is soon liquidated?

definitions.text: Coastal defence that is soon liquidated?

parts.words: Coastal defence that is soon liquidated
parts.note: a fortification on the beach, built by children, that the incoming tide soon washes away

explanation.surface: A military history note about shoreline fortifications that are quickly wound up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liquidated' suggests being wiped out or wound up as a business; here it is literal, turned to slush by the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A child's turreted mound on the beach is a mock fortress, dissolved by the tide within hours.

clue.text: The Italian sun-fish

explanation.surface: A menu offering an Italian dish of sunfish.
explanation.walkthrough: The Italian word for sun is this, and it is also a flatfish.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian for the sun in the sky is this word; it is also a flat sea fish such as Dover's.

clue.text: Even the short-sighted could see it was dangerous

definitions.text: Even the short-sighted could see it was dangerous

parts.words: Even the short-sighted could see it was dangerous
parts.note: an object close by is visible to the myopic, but the phrase means a narrow escape

explanation.surface: A remark that a hazard was obvious to anyone, even someone with poor eyesight.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow escape is a close call, and a close object is one the short-sighted could see.

clue.text: Best substitute for shaving soap

explanation.surface: Advice that the finest thing to use instead of shaving soap is something else.
explanation.definitionFit: The pick of a group is its top layer, like the richest part of milk; a lather product for shaving comes in this form.

clue.text: Pale and shy, perhaps, but attractive looking

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the letters of pale and shy might be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: A description of someone who is wan and timid but good-looking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges PALE and SHY.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-proportioned figure is good to look at, so the word describes an appealing form.

clue.text: Declines to give oral classes

indicators.note: oral means spoken, so the word for classes is heard rather than read

parts.note: lessons are classes taught at school

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to teach spoken-language classes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Declines' looks like refuses; it means diminishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that declines grows smaller or weaker, i.e. diminishes.

clue.text: Guns recoil in game

indicators.note: the guns spring back, so the slang word for them is read backwards

parts.note: gats is slang for guns or pistols

explanation.surface: Firearms kick back during a shoot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recoil' turns GATS around.
explanation.definitionFit: A male deer is hunted, and hunted animals are game.

clue.text: Skirt hem raised above the knee

definitions.text: Skirt hem raised above the knee

parts.words: Skirt hem raised above the knee
parts.note: a short skirt shows the part of the leg between hip and knee

explanation.surface: A fashion note about a miniskirt's shortened hemline.
explanation.definitionFit: The upper leg lies between hip and knee, which a raised skirt reveals.

clue.text: Speak about nothing in particular

parts.note: to talk without specifics, in broad terms, rather than idle chit-chat

explanation.surface: Making small talk on no subject at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests chit-chat; the meaning is talking in broad, non-specific terms.
explanation.definitionFit: To talk in broad terms is to avoid anything specific, i.e. about nothing particular.

clue.text: A quick drop for one waiting for opening time

definitions.text: A quick drop for one waiting for opening time

parts.words: A quick drop for one waiting for opening time
parts.note: a skydiver plummets before pulling the parachute open, not a drinker waiting for the pub

explanation.surface: A pub-goer having a swift drink before the bar opens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening time' suggests British pub hours and 'drop' a drink; the opening is a parachute's.
explanation.definitionFit: Skydivers plummet unchecked before the parachute opens, which is the drop described.

clue.text: Permission to proceed

explanation.surface: A note granting someone the go-ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Being allowed is having consent, as in shore leave; to depart is to set off or go.

clue.text: Such a declaration is treason, in a way

indicators.note: in a way signals that the letters of is treason come out in a different order

explanation.surface: A claim that a certain statement amounts to betrayal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a way' rearranges IS TREASON.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm statement or claim is a declaration of something as fact.

clue.text: Impressed by eastern flight

parts.note: something impressed is stamped with a mark

explanation.surface: Someone moved by the sight of a migration of eastern birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' means fleeing, not air travel.
explanation.definitionFit: A panicked rush of a herd is a headlong fleeing.

clue.text: What might be there to put you out?

definitions.text: What might be there to put you out?

indicators.note: might be signals that the letters of there could be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A question about what could be present to send you to sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might be' rearranges THERE into an old anaesthetic, which puts a patient out.
explanation.definitionFit: An old anaesthetic gas renders a patient unconscious.

clue.text: Extricated from dilemma near the Dutch coast

explanation.surface: Someone freed from a tricky spot while sailing by Holland.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hook of Holland is a Dutch port and headland, so a ship near it is offshore of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Escaping trouble is like a fish freed from a barb; a vessel lying beside the Dutch headland is just offshore of it.

clue.text: A good distance, but not too far for a drive

definitions.text: not too far for a drive

explanation.surface: A long trip, though not too far to go by car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drive' is the opening golf shot, which aims for the mown strip between tee and green.
explanation.definitionFit: Quite a stretch is a reasonable distance; in golf the mown strip lies within a tee shot's reach.

clue.text: Using force with a quarter taking a break

parts.note: W for west is one of the four compass quarters

explanation.surface: Applying force alongside someone who is pausing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulling something away by violent twisting is to employ force.

clue.text: Caught in something afoot — it's a disgrace!

indicators.note: in places the letter for caught inside the footwear

parts.note: a sandal is something worn on the foot
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone caught up in a shady plot, which is shameful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'afoot' suggests something happening; here it is footwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A public outrage or shameful affair is a disgrace.

clue.text: Sea-going vandal

explanation.surface: A seafaring hooligan.
explanation.definitionFit: A fast naval warship is a sea-going vessel; a wrecker who smashes things is a vandal.

clue.text: I take key and lock out wild animal

indicators.note: out places the lock of hair outside the other letters

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: A keeper takes the key and locks a wild beast out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lock out' suggests barring a door; here the lock is hair, placed outside I and G.
explanation.definitionFit: A female big cat is a fierce wild creature.

clue.text: Naval man, opposite to a landlady?

definitions.text: Naval man, opposite to a landlady?

parts.words: Naval man, opposite to a landlady
parts.note: swap land for its opposite and lady for its male counterpart to name a senior admiral

explanation.surface: A sailor lodging opposite his landlady.
explanation.walkthrough: A senior admiral on the British Admiralty Board has this title.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior officer on the Admiralty Board is a top naval figure.

clue.text: Listens out for recruits

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of listens are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone listens out for new recruits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges LISTENS.
explanation.definitionFit: Signing up people for the forces is to recruit them.

clue.text: Rent it leasehold, retaining name

indicators.note: retaining shows that the phrase rent it leasehold keeps the word within it

explanation.surface: Advice to let a property on a lease while keeping its name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retaining' signals the word kept in rENT IT LEasehold.
explanation.definitionFit: To give a title to something is to call or designate it.

clue.text: Precise demand

explanation.surface: An exact demand.
explanation.definitionFit: Accurate means precise; to insist on payment is to require or demand it.

clue.text: Athenian garret

explanation.surface: A Greek loft.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to Attica, the region of Athens; also a room in the roof space.

clue.text: Skill shown when skill is added to effort

parts.note: art is skill, as in the art of persuasion
a try is an effort or attempt

explanation.surface: A saying that talent shows when ability is combined with hard work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'added to' joins the pieces in order: ART, IS, then TRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Great craftsmanship and creative talent amount to skill.

clue.text: A brace affected gait

explanation.surface: A pretentious walk with a support.
explanation.definitionFit: A strengthening bar is a brace; a swaggering walk is an affected gait.

clue.text: County people retire to

explanation.surface: A shire where people go to retire.
explanation.walkthrough: Bedfordshire is an English county, abbreviated to this.
explanation.definitionFit: The short form of Bedfordshire is an English shire; at night people go to sleep in these.

clue.text: Not in duplicate — that's definite!

explanation.surface: A copy that is clearly not included.
explanation.definitionFit: Not in twice gives the pair joined by a conjunction; the phrase means thorough or utter.

clue.text: Reach the same sound conclusion

parts.note: two words ending in matching sounds, not people agreeing on a sensible verdict

explanation.surface: Two people arrive at the same sensible verdict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' suggests sensible; it means sound literally, at word endings.
explanation.definitionFit: Words that end on matching sounds, like cat and hat, share a final sound.

clue.text: The thrill one may get playing football

explanation.surface: The excitement a footballer gets from the game.
explanation.definitionFit: A buzz of excitement is a thrill; striking the ball with the foot is a football action.

clue.text: Exciting experiences coming — sure to be special

parts.note: an advent is a coming or arrival

indicators.note: special signals that the letters of sure are made into something different

explanation.surface: Thrilling times are on the way, sure to be out of the ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'special' rearranges SURE into URES after ADVENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Daring escapades are thrilling episodes in life.
